subject: Acme Systems — private deployment IaC kickoff and review
messages:
From: Simon Welch <simon.welch@acme-systems.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-systems.com
Date: Sat, 4 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — IaC review request and constraints

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the earlier call. Per our discussion, were preparing to onboard Redwood for a private deployment into a mix of VPC-connected cloud hardware and our on-prem rack (air-gapped segments). Before we start procurement, we need Redwood to do an infrastructure-as-code review of the modules and CI gating we plan to use.

Requested items:
- Review Terraform modules for VPC peering, subnet zoning, and node pools (well send TF state outputs).
- Verify Helm charts and values schema for the operator + ingress + observability stack.
- Confirm Ansible playbooks for on-prem bootstrap (PXE -> OS -> kubeadm flow) are idempotent and include secret handling guidance.
- Check CI/CD gating: static analysis, terratest/Terraform validate steps, and canary rollout config.

Attached: acme-privstack-requirements.pdf, network-zones.csv.

Target timeline: joint technical review next week (flexible). Go-live target: Aug 15. Please include any security/compliance asks up front so we can align procurement.

Simon
Simon Welch
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Systems
sim.welch@acme-systems.com

---

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Simon Welch <simon.welch@acme-systems.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — IaC review request and constraints

Hi Simon,

Thanks for the clear list — we can run a focused joint review. Proposed next steps and agenda:
1) Pre-review: well intake your TF plan outputs and Helm values. Dev will do an initial pass for obvious blockers.
2) Joint session (90 min): architecture diagram walkthrough, module ownership, CI job review, and rollout gating.
3) Deliverables: prioritized issues (P0/P1), required fixes for security gating, and a checklist for procurement.

Please drop the architecture diagram into the Drive link (or share a Visio/PDF). Ive attached our internal "redwood-priv-iac-checklist.md" which lists the items we typically validate.

Proposed time windows: Tue 2026-07-07 09:00-11:00 PT or Wed 2026-07-08 13:00-15:00 PT. Which works for your infra + procurement folks?

Also: can you confirm whether on-prem requires SR-IOV for NIC passthrough (weve seen this affect CNI choices), and whether any PVCs must be provisioned from a proprietary SAN that requires custom storage classes? Those details change our recommended Helm values and terraform modules.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-priv-iac-checklist.md

---

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Simon Welch <simon.welch@acme-systems.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Jul 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — IaC review request and constraints

Simon / Mina / Olga,

Quick technical notes ahead of the joint session: we pulled the sample TF plan outputs you uploaded and did a light scan. High-level findings (Dev quick-pass):
- Terraform module layout: looks modular but were missing a clear separation between networking (vpc/subnets/route-tables) and compute (nodepools/autoscaling). Recommend moving compute into a separate registry module to allow isolated fast cycles.
- CNI recommendation: if SR-IOV is required, well recommend using a CNI that supports device plugin (Multus + sriov-cni), otherwise we prefer Calico for policy + BPF dataplane for perf.
- Storage: if your SAN requires specific provisioner, we need a StorageClass template and an example PVC test that runs during CI (attaches, writes 1GB, verifies read).
- Helm charts: values.yaml currently includes environment secrets in plain keys (e.g., global.secrets.*). Suggest switching to sealed-secrets/KMS integration and adding explicit secretRef fields to values schema.
- CI gating: please ensure pipelines include terraform fmt/tflint/validate, terragrunt (if used) checks, terratest or kitchen-terraform for critical modules, and a non-destructive plan approval step (PR comment with plan output). For Helm, run helm lint + chart-testing and a dry-run install into a throwaway namespace.

Ive left inline comments on the GitHub branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-deploy-modules/pull/78 — key diffs include a new module boundary and a sample GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/priv-deploy-ci.yml). Also attaching a small tf plan output snippet for reference.

Questions for Acme before we lock the checklist:
- Expected number of nodes per cluster and expected peak qps/latency targets (affects node sizing and CVM memory tuning).
- Any air-gapped constraints for the initial OS image build (we may need to provide an offline bundle).

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
Attachment: tf-plan-outputs.txt

---

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Simon Welch <simon.welch@acme-systems.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — IaC review request and constraints

Simon/Team,

A couple of high-level governance items from product security and infra leadership:
- All TF modules that run with elevated permissions must have an owner and a documented rollback path. Please add an OWNERS file in each module.
- CI must enforce the following gates before a module can be applied in prod: tflint pass, terraform validate, terratest (smoke), KMS access verification, and a secrets-scan stage.
- For canary deployments of control-plane or operator changes, require automatic rollback when X% error threshold met in the first 10 minutes; we will supply a small canary harness that integrates with your observability stack.

Operational ask: supply one person from Acme to be the module owner/contact for post-merge handoffs. Procurement can handle contract sign-off; we want a single technical lead to avoid paging issues during rollout.

Ive attached our internal security checklist for private stacks (security-checklist.xlsx) — its intentionally terse but maps to the items above.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Platform Engineering, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
Attachment: security-checklist.xlsx

---

From: Simon Welch <simon.welch@acme-systems.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-systems.com, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — IaC review request and constraints

Thanks team — that all looks good and very thorough. We can do Tue 2026-07-07 09:00 PT; Ive asked Rachel from procurement to join and shell handle the contract touches.

Answers to outstanding questions:
- Node sizing: initial clusters will be 6 nodes (mish-mix of 8x40GB and 4x96GB) with a target peak of ~12k qps for the most latency-sensitive path.
- Air-gapped builds: yes — we need an offline bundle for the initial OS image.
- SR-IOV: not required for v1, but we may enable it for a subset of workloads later.
- Storage: SAN requires a custom provisioner; well share the vendor driver and example StorageClass before the session.

Ive also routed the DocuSign envelope for the statement of work; procurement will complete that this week. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/link/ACME-SIGNATURE-12345

See you on Tue.

Simon
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Systems
sim.welch@acme-systems.com
